svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "DNA is a double helix of two antiparallel strands. Each strand has a sugar\u2013phosphate backbone; the bases pair A\u2013T (two hydrogen bonds) and C\u2013G (three)."], [3, "Helicase unwinds the helix and unzips the two strands by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the bases. Each strand becomes a template."], [6.5, "Free nucleotides pair with the exposed bases by complementary base pairing: A with T, C with G."], [9.5, "DNA polymerase joins the nucleotides into new strands, only in the 5\u2032\u21923\u2032 direction: continuously on the leading strand, in short Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand. DNA ligase joins the fragments."], [13, "Two DNA molecules, identical to each other and to the original. Each has one original strand and one new strand: semi-conservative replication."]]
svg.title: DNA structure and replication
svg.desc: Chromosome, double helix and a nucleotide, then a section of DNA with antiparallel strands, sugar-phosphate backbones and complementary base pairs, replicated by helicase, DNA polymerase and ligase.
svg.text: Left: from chromosome to nucleotide. Right: DNA drawn flat (the real molecule is a helix). Not to scale.

g.data-info: One very long DNA molecule, coiled round proteins (histones) and supercoiled. Seen as two chromatids after replication.
Two strands of DNA twisted round each other, held together by hydrogen bonds between the bases.
Part of every nucleotide. Phosphates and sugars join alternately to form the sugar–phosphate backbone.
A 5-carbon sugar in each DNA nucleotide (RNA has ribose instead).
Adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) or guanine (G). The order of bases is the genetic code.
The strong outer “rails” of each strand, joined by covalent bonds. Dark: an original strand; orange: a new strand.
A always pairs with T, and C with G: a purine with a pyrimidine, so the rungs are all the same width.
Weak bonds between the bases: two between A and T, three between C and G. Easily broken for replication and transcription.
The two strands run in opposite directions: one 5′→3′, the other 3′→5′.
Nucleotides in the nucleus that pair with the exposed bases of each template strand.
The strong outer “rails” of each strand, joined by covalent bonds. Dark: an original strand; orange: a new strand.
Joins the short Okazaki fragments of the lagging strand into one continuous strand.
Enzyme that unwinds the double helix and separates the strands by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the bases.
Enzyme that joins free nucleotides to the growing new strand, using the old strand as a template. It can only add nucleotides in the 5′→3′ direction.
